newsitem.title: EGYPT: Lack of reforms hinders Mideast economy growth - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Lack of reforms hinders Mideast economy growth - IMF.

text.p: Foreign investors focus more on economic reform than on progress towards peace in deciding whether to pour money into the Middle East, International Monetary Fund officials said on Monday.

"Regional peace certainly reduces perceptions of risk but not enough to improve investment. Economic reforms are the key," Mohammed el-Erian, of the IMF's Middle East and North Africa Department, told a news conference.
Stanley Fischer, managing director of the IMF, said regional economic conferences such as the one opening in Cairo on Tuesday, help countries speed up their economic overhaul programmes.

"It has a role, not a dominant role, but a role in sending the message that there's a world out there waiting for the region to join it," he said about the Cairo gathering of some 2,000 participants from 92 countries.
Fischer said "investments are the signal and cause of slow growth in the region...fiscal and trade reforms must be implemented to increase growth."
Citing a regional report, Fischer said direct foreign investment in the Middle East and North Africa region was lower than in all other parts of the world except Africa.

The IMF -- which advises countries on economic reforms -- has put foreign investment in the Middle East and North Africa in 1994 at less than 1.0 percent of gross domestic product, compared to almost 1.5 percent in Asia.

Fischer said the economies of Israel and Palestinian self-rule areas were the most affected by the slow pace of peace negotiations but investment in other Middle East and North Africa countries was hampered more by local policies.
"What is happening to the peace process is extremely unfortunate and will adversely affect the growth of some countries in the region, especially Israel and the Gaza self-rule area," Fischer said.

"But it has a smaller impact on those countries farther afield...Let's put it that way, we wouldn't make different economic policy recommendations to any country in the region based on the progress in the peace process."
Many Arab countries attending the Cairo conference have said balanced Arab-Israeli peace is a precondition to any economic cooperation with the Jewish state.
Israel's right-wing government is currently locked in negotiations with the PLO on implementing a long-overdue Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.
